stories.title: Supreme Court Drops 5-4 Ruling In Trump Ballroom Fight
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court, in an unsigned 5-4 order, cleared the way for construction of President Donald Trump’s $400 million White House ballroom to continue, blocking lower-court rulings that would have halted aboveground work. The decision replaced a temporary order issued earlier in August. Chief Justice John Roberts dissented, writing that the construction was likely unlawful.

The court ruled that prosecutors had failed to prove the defendants’ guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

stories.title: Tim Cook’s parting message: Apple is in the hands of a product builder
stories.summary: In a farewell memo to Apple employees, outgoing chief executive Tim Cook presented successor John Ternus as an experienced product builder. Cook highlighted Ternus’s work across major Apple hardware lines including the iPhone, Mac and AirPods.

stories.title: Trump attacks datacenter backlash, claiming communities pushing back risk becoming ‘backwards and poor’
stories.summary: Donald Trump criticised US communities opposing local datacentre projects, warning that those rejecting them risk becoming “backwards and poor.” The comments came amid growing controversy over proposed facilities in election campaigns before the November midterms. A recent poll cited by The Guardian found that three-quarters of Americans opposed having datacentres built next to their homes.

stories.title: ‘Superhuman’ AI tool spots heart disease in less than 2 seconds
stories.summary: Doctors have developed an AI system that can identify heart disease from a routine electrocardiogram in under two seconds. Trained on data from millions of patients, the tool extracts patterns from ECGs that the human eye may not detect. Its developers say it could help fast-track high-risk patients for treatment.

stories.title: Rise of Chicken Shop Date highlights how YouTube turned the tables on TV
stories.summary: Amelia Dimoldenberg’s YouTube interview series Chicken Shop Date has grown from a show that struggled to attract mainstream celebrities into one able to choose among A-list guests. Its success illustrates how YouTube formats and creators have gained influence once held by traditional television. Dimoldenberg said publicists ignored the mock-date show for years before its audience and status grew.
